title: Hugging Face Hands Chat Routing to OpenRouter Integration
summary: Hugging Face retired its inference router on Nov 16, 2026, routing all Hub chat requests through OpenRouter's 160-model network with failover and sync.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Hugging Face retired its custom inference router on November 16, 2026, routing all Hub language-model requests through OpenRouter instead.
- The integration spans 160 models from 38 labs with live price and speed stats, automatic failover, and request-log sync.
- OpenRouter reports open-weight model share jumped from 27 percent to 72 percent in under a year, positioning itself as open AI's routing standard.


Hugging Face retired its custom inference router on November 16, 2026, handing all language-model chat requests on the Hub to OpenRouter's provider network. The integration spans 160 models from 38 labs, delivering per-request provider selection, live price and speed statistics, automatic failover, and request-log synchronization into users' own Hugging Face storage. Existing Hugging Face API tokens and code continue to work without modification, ensuring backward compatibility for developers.


## What Changed on the Hub


Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue announced the switch in a November 16 post, explaining that the platform's previous routing layer has been replaced by OpenRouter's infrastructure. Chat inference calls originating on the Hub now flow through OpenRouter's multi-provider network, which monitors latency, cost, and uptime across dozens of endpoints. When a provider experiences downtime or slow response times, OpenRouter automatically reroutes requests to alternative hosts running the same model, reducing request failures and improving user experience for applications built on Hugging Face endpoints.


Request logs and trace data generated by OpenRouter sync directly into each user's Hugging Face storage, preserving auditability and compliance workflows. Developers retain full visibility into which provider handled each request, the tokens consumed, and the round-trip latency. The migration required no client-side code changes because Hugging Face maintained its existing API surface while swapping the backend router.


## Open-Weight Model Adoption Accelerates


OpenRouter CEO Alex Atallah disclosed that open-weight model usage on the platform climbed from 27 percent to 72 percent in under a year, framing the Hugging Face partnership as a natural evolution for open AI infrastructure. The routing layer now serves requests for models such as Llama, Mistral, Qwen, and dozens of others, with real-time metrics on cost per million tokens and median response time visible to developers before they dispatch a request. This transparency allows teams to optimize spend and performance without locking into a single provider.


The shift reflects broader momentum in the open-model ecosystem, where multiple hosting providers compete on price and reliability rather than model exclusivity. By aggregating these providers under a unified routing API, OpenRouter and Hugging Face aim to deliver the same developer experience users expect from closed-platform vendors while preserving the flexibility and cost advantages of open weights.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 16, 2026, the OpenRouter integration is live for all Hugging Face Hub users. No opt-in or migration step is required, and existing inference endpoints continue to resolve without interruption. Developers who previously called Hugging Face's inference API now benefit from OpenRouter's failover logic and provider diversity automatically, with no changes to authentication or request formatting.


## What This Means


The Hugging Face-OpenRouter integration consolidates the open-model routing layer under a single platform, reducing infrastructure fragmentation and improving uptime for production applications. For developers, the change translates to lower request-failure rates, transparent cost comparisons, and seamless access to 160 models without managing multiple provider accounts. As open-weight share continues to climb, this partnership positions OpenRouter as the de facto gateway for open AI inference, while Hugging Face focuses on model hosting, training tooling, and community collaboration rather than maintaining its own routing middleware.
